comments.content: At that time we didn't have a clear scope of what to fuzz. Now we have the [LibUbiquityPool](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/a1b11e1b944227144d7cc19ab320220d9fce8b69/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibUbiquityPool.sol) which is going to be deployed on mainnet, so the contract scope is clear.

I think that auditors from our 1st Sherlock audit have already performed all of the fuzz, invariant and formal verification tests so it makes sense to set a normal priority for:
- https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/issues/925
- https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/issues/563
- https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/issues/926
Sounds good. The same "properties" could be later converted to [invariants](https://book.getfoundry.sh/forge/invariant-testing).

We should implement fuzzing tests for [LibUbiquityPool](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/a1b11e1b944227144d7cc19ab320220d9fce8b69/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibUbiquityPool.sol). I think it would be enough to fuzz only "user scenarios":
- [Dollar token mint](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/a1b11e1b944227144d7cc19ab320220d9fce8b69/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibUbiquityPool.sol#L486)
- [Dollar token redeem](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/a1b11e1b944227144d7cc19ab320220d9fce8b69/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibUbiquityPool.sol#L594)
- [collecting redemption](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/a1b11e1b944227144d7cc19ab320220d9fce8b69/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibUbiquityPool.sol#L710)
Possible solutions for fuzzing tests (I would simply start with foundry since we're using it as a development framework + it also contains invariant testing):
- https://book.getfoundry.sh/forge/fuzz-testing
- https://github.com/crytic/echidna
- https://github.com/crytic/medusa
What should be done:
1. Impelent fuzzing tests for the scenarios described above (you may create them in a separate test file like `UbiquityPoolFacet.fuzz.t.sol` so we could distinguish unit and fuzz tests)
2. Setup testing CI this way:
a) On PR fuzzing tests should run with a small number of runs (so that we could merge PRs fast)
b) On merge to the `development` branch fuzzing tests should run with a great number of runs to test many cases (keep in mind that github action runnners can run for 6 hours)

@gitcoindev How did you come up with the `90000` number? By default it is [set](https://book.getfoundry.sh/reference/config/testing#max_test_rejects) to `65536`. Why do we need to increase it to this exact number?
This seems to be a low severity issue but keeping in mind that nobody from the Sherlock audit have reported this bug it seems that nobody fuzzed the `UbiquityPoolFacet` contract extensively.

@gitcoindev 
1. Could you add 2 more fuzz tests:
a) If user mints X Dollars he gets exactly X Dollars (minus fee)
b) If user redeems X Dollars exactly X Dollars are subtracted from user balance
2. Pls notice the original issue spec also describe setting up CI
Overall the PR looks great, we will iterate on the fuzzing tests later

@gitcoindev Did you experiment with how long the deep fuzz [workflow](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/64ab8b9e378abe7cc019924bd43e7891d6d9d884/.github/workflows/deep-fuzz.yml) runs for, let's say, `1_000_000` [runs](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/64ab8b9e378abe7cc019924bd43e7891d6d9d884/packages/contracts/foundry.toml#L44) ? I want to find out a value so that deep fuzz workflow could run for the amount of hours close to github max CI limit (6 hours).
